answer: To enforce Sybil resistance, an AI agent network mandates cryptographic hardware attestations bound to physical compute infrastructure. Any unbacked identity is a mere fable, as nodes must continuously prove control over physical hardware—down to the copper trace delays in silicon—via trusted execution environments. By anchoring voting weight across the agent nebula directly to verifiable physical capital, an attacker incurs linear hardware acquisition costs, rendering large-scale identity spoofing economically irrational.
